clue.text: Recoil from bribe

definitions.meaning: a gun's backward jolt on firing is its recoil
an illicit payment slipped back to someone who arranged a deal

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the jolt of a fired gun, and a secret illegal payment.

clue.text: Principal directors needed facility to provide notes

parts.note: key means principal or most important
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: The top directors insisted on an amenity for issuing memos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests memos but means musical notes on a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano's row of keys is the apparatus a player uses to sound musical tones.

clue.text: Skilled workers put together vessel's pieces

parts.note: a craft is a vessel or boat; with its 's
chessmen, the pieces in a game, are men

explanation.surface: Artisans assemble the parts of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess and draughts the pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen are artisans who practise a trade with skill.

clue.text: Number in huge Egyptian celebration

indicators.note: the number's abbreviation sits inside the word for huge

parts.note: big means huge
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian, as in Egyptian pounds

explanation.surface: A large Egyptian festival draws a great number of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of indulgent revelry, a spree or party.

clue.text: Acclaimed and honoured internationally with Nobel finally clinched

indicators.note: to clinch is to grip tightly, so the end of Nobel is held within

parts.note: a player capped has been selected to play for their country

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of Nobel

explanation.surface: A scientist was praised and fêted worldwide after finally securing a Nobel prize.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport, a cap marks selection for a national team.
explanation.definitionFit: Being applauded by an audience is a form of being acclaimed.

clue.text: Representations setting motorway back by years

indicators.note: with 'back', setting a thing back turns it round, so the motorway's letters are read in reverse
completes 'setting ... back', telling us to read the motorway's letters backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's best-known motorway, written here as MI
ages means a very long time, many years

explanation.surface: Someone describes pictures of a motorway project being delayed by years.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway running north from London; Britain numbers its motorways M1, M2 and so on, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures and likenesses are representations of what they show.

clue.text: Animals collected with various game round new lake

indicators.note: the jumbled letters of game go round the abbreviation for new
various suggests differing forms, so the letters of game appear in a mixed order

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A zoo's collection is assembled from assorted wildlife near a newly made lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the letters of game into a jumble that 'round' places around N; Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild creatures kept for show.

clue.text: Relish nothing more than a breath of fresh air

parts.words: more than a breath of fresh air
parts.note: a gust of wind is stronger than a mere breath of air
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone says they enjoy nothing better than a breath of fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment, the same sense as relish as a noun.

clue.text: Musicians' exercises with direction in prescribed form

indicators.note: exercises and direction both go inside the prescribed form

parts.note: a set form is fixed or prescribed, as in a set piece
PT, physical training, means exercises
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A band's practice drills follow a standard routine with a conductor's guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: PT is physical training, the school gym lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of seven players is a septet, a set of musicians.

clue.text: Reluctant to enter church in cloak

indicators.note: the word for reluctant goes in between the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
loth (or loath) means unwilling

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is reluctant to come in wearing a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloak someone is to wrap or dress them, a verb sense of covering in garments.

clue.text: Long story without point

indicators.note: an old sense of without is outside, so the story goes round the point

parts.note: a yarn is a tall tale or story
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tedious tale that rambles on without making any point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside': YARN surrounds E.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave or pine for it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Collapse and sell up completely

indicators.note: a collapse brings a structure down in disorder, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A failing business owner is told to fold and sell off everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collapse' looks like the definition but signals the anagram of AND SELL UP.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in every respect or totally, as in being beaten thoroughly.

clue.text: In a predicament as honest error repelled head

indicators.note: an error is a mistake, so the letters of honest come out wrongly arranged
something repelled is driven back, so the head's synonym is read backwards

parts.note: the top of something is its head

explanation.surface: Someone is in a fix because an honest mistake drove off their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges the letters of honest, and 'repelled' turns the synonym for head round; 'In a predicament' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put on the spot is idiom for being in a difficult or awkward position.

clue.text: Silly person cooking this bird ruins plan

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'to cook someone's ...' means to spoil their plans, so this is the bird in that saying

explanation.definitionFit: The farmyard bird is also a slang word for a fool, and appears in the idiom about spoiled schemes.

clue.text: Found out, as Uriah was, in a way

indicators.note: the dropped-aitch word sits inside the abbreviation for a way, so in marks containment

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
Uriah Heep in Dickens's David Copperfield calls himself 'umble, dropping the h of humble

explanation.surface: Someone was exposed as a fraud, rather like Dickens's Uriah Heep.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep, the scheming clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield, is forever 'umble'; that sits inside RD for road.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rumbled is British slang for having one's deception discovered.

clue.text: Writing characters into the script?

parts.note: seems to mean a dramatist adding roles to a play, but means forming the letters of a script, as a signwriter does

explanation.definitionFit: Lettering is the craft or result of inscribing alphabetic characters, as in a sign.

clue.text: Corrective efforts when deserter's apprehended in time

indicators.note: a person apprehended is caught and held, so the deserter is held inside the period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is someone who deserts their side; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A runaway soldier is caught, and remedial action follows just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of errata is printed to correct mistakes in a book, a remedial effort.

clue.text: Try to put off casual worker with no increment

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
O, zero, means no or nothing
a rise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: A temporary worker is fobbed off without a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to stall or delay a decision in order to gain time.

clue.text: One hoping to take game and depart deliriously with gold

indicators.note: something done deliriously is wild and disordered, so the letters of depart are scrambled

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A poacher wants to bag game and dash off wildly with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting animal seeks to catch prey, as a predator does.

clue.text: Kidnapping in US succeeded, of course, briefly

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
natch is breezy slang standing in for naturally, that is of course

explanation.surface: A news item about an abduction in America that went off, naturally, without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kidnapping in US' is the definition: the American underworld calls an abduction this.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang a snatch is an abduction or kidnap.

clue.text: Seat for Jumbo pilot who had shakes

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things, so the letters of who had are rearranged

explanation.surface: An airline captain who had the jitters climbs into his seat on a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo pilot' suggests an airliner captain; here Jumbo is an elephant and the pilot its mahout.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is the canopied seat carried on an elephant's back for its rider.

clue.text: Appropriate vessel for Cook?

parts.note: reads as the ship for the explorer Captain Cook, but is also a pan in which a cook prepares vegetables with vapour

explanation.definitionFit: A steam-driven ship is a vessel, and so is the kitchen pan that cooks food over boiling water.

clue.text: Upset about article, but you'll have to accept it

definitions.text: but you'll have to accept it

indicators.note: the word for upset goes around the article, as about means surrounding

parts.note: sore means upset or aggrieved
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about a newspaper piece, but is told to live with it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a defiant retort meaning the matter is settled whether you like it or not.

clue.text: Held up as railway service (of top quality) departs

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway
an ace in tennis is an unreturnable serve, a top-quality service
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A train was delayed as the luxury rail service pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' suggests a delayed train, but means supported.
explanation.definitionFit: Something braced is propped or supported, held up by a strut.

clue.text: Lead removed from toy gun

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front letter, which is taken away here

parts.note: to toy with something is to trifle with it

explanation.surface: Someone takes the lead pellets out of a toy pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests the metal of bullets but means the first letter; TRIFLE loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled firearm with a grooved bore is a type of gun.

clue.text: Shakespearean clown's singular entry in public entertainment

indicators.note: the singular letter makes its entry into the word for public entertainment

parts.note: a fete is an outdoor public festival
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A comic actor makes an unusual appearance at a public show.
explanation.walkthrough: A fete is a British summer outdoor fundraiser with stalls and games.
explanation.definitionFit: Feste is the witty jester in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Slogan resulting from discussion with hunter, perhaps

parts.note: a hunter is a pocket timepiece with a hinged cover, an example of a watch
to have a word with someone is to have a discussion

explanation.surface: A rallying cry emerges from talks with a man who hunts.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter is a type of pocket watch with a protective lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto or rallying phrase adopted by a group is its slogan.

clue.text: Agitated male workers getting little money

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
TU is a trade union, a body of workers
p is a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: Male staff are upset at receiving only small change.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up or flustered is the informal sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Reprove players taking single in front of wicket, say

indicators.note: one piece comes before the next, so the single and the players precede the wicket

parts.note: the cast of a play are its players
I, the Roman numeral one, is a single
a wicket is a small gate, so a gate is an example

explanation.surface: A cricket team is told off for scoring a single in front of the wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture misleads: a wicket is also a small gate, as in a wicket gate.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke severely, a stronger synonym of reprove.

clue.text: International volunteers going in first in unpleasant spot

indicators.note: the volunteers enter at the front, so their letters come before the international's

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: International volunteers lead the way into a nasty trouble spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or stain, a mark of something bad.

clue.text: Doctor has to move carefully to operate on bed

parts.note: to edge is to move slowly and cautiously

explanation.surface: A surgeon must proceed cautiously when operating on a patient in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operate on bed' suggests surgery, but the bed is a riverbed or seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging scoops mud from the bottom of a river or harbour.

clue.text: Harvest fruit crop up again

parts.note: to reap is to harvest a crop
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A farmer harvests the fruit crop once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop' seems to belong with the harvest, but 'crop up' is the verb of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To crop up again is to show up once more, to return into view.
